review.semantic_boundary:
# Frozen semantic boundary

PR8 requires encoder cache allocation, eviction, capacity planning and scheduling in actual embedding-row units, with correct ordered reads across prompt windows and speculative lookahead. The repair observes the real scheduler compute_encoder_budget and runner MultiModalBudget using a real registry/profiler path. Only the media input producer and processor-cache creation are controlled. SchedulerConfig is constructed for real: the grader uses a one-token decoder batch and the independent challenge uses two tokens, so expected capacities retain the constructor-derived floor as max(batch limit, embedding rows). Zero remaining runtime encoder resources are exercised separately by the existing admission/lifecycle tests. A registry may expose different default prompt and explicit embedding coordinate accessors; actual consumer budgets determine correctness. Fresh observations and existing encoder-write/cache/read transitions remain in the grading path. Independent capacity challenges use different lengths and masks. Saved Astra tracked and untracked source is a legal alternate implementation; scheduler-only and runner-only prompt-context regressions are negative controls.

The grading observer uses a real SchedulerConfig with a one-token decoder batch; the independent challenge uses a two-token batch and different media geometry. Both preserve the constructor-derived capacity floor. Model metadata, media-input production and processor-cache creation are controlled; scheduling, registry profiling and runner capacity consumers execute real code. Existing low-resource runtime admission, actual encoder writes, cache lifecycle and partial reads remain exercised.

The task statement is three natural prose paragraphs. Environment recipes, dependency locks and the Oracle patch are unchanged by this repair. Saved Astra source is a preserved implementation control, not a new model rollout or a reconstruction of the original root filesystem. Raw current results and superseded attempts are recorded separately in e2e-evidence.json.
